{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Given extreme max value (201.39) vs mean (2.81), consider log-transform or robust ANOVA if residuals non-normal.",
    "For Success: Binary outcome (0/1) violates ANOVA normality/homoscedasticity assumptions. Use logistic regression or Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test with paradigm as predictor. Chi-square test of independence as omnibus test alternative.",
    "For Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Extremely right-skewed (max=29.82 vs mean=0.47) suggests log-transform or non-parametric alternative (Kruskal-Wallis).",
    "For Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Moderate right skew (max=75.35 vs mean=12.50) warrants checking residuals; consider transformation if needed.",
    "For AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Bounded [0,1] with mean 0.38 suggests beta regression or arcsin-sqrt transform if variance near boundaries differs."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assumed via experimental design; verify no temporal autocorrelation within mice.",
    "Normality: Shapiro-Wilk or Q-Q plots on residuals for each continuous variable; severe violations expected for Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test across paradigms; unequal n (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505) reduces power for variance comparisons.",
    "Sample size: Total n=76655 provides excellent power, but extreme group imbalance (Combined: 63.7% of data) inflates Type I error for unequal variance cases.",
    "Outliers: Winsorize or exclude observations beyond 3SD after transformation for Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target given extreme max values."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA significant (p<0.05): Tukey HSD for pairwise comparisons among 5 paradigms, controlling familywise error.",
    "If unequal variances: Games-Howell test for pairwise comparisons.",
    "If non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis used: Dunn's test with Bonferroni correction.",
    "For Success (logistic): Marginal means from logistic regression with Tukey-adjusted comparisons, or pairwise Fisher's exact tests with Bonferroni correction.",
    "Focus comparisons: Combined vs all single-modality conditions; Sham vs active stimulation conditions."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined condition likely shows fastest Time-to-Target, highest Success rate, and best Path Efficiency given largest sample size and presumed optimal stimulation.",
    "Sham condition expected to show poorest performance (slowest Time-to-Target, lowest Success, highest AD indicating more erratic paths).",
    "ICMS Only vs Visual Only conditions may differ: ICMS may enhance speed/efficiency while visual conditions show paradigm-dependent effects (Dim vs Bright).",
    "AD expected to inversely correlate with Path Efficiency and Success across paradigms.",
    "Average Speed may show less paradigm differentiation than accuracy/efficiency metrics."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe group imbalance: Combined (63.7%) vs Sham (4.6%) and Bright Visual Only (4.3%) limits precision for small groups.",
    "No mouse-level random effect specified: Repeated measures within 8 mice violate independence assumption; mixed-effects model with Mouse as random intercept preferred.",
    "Cross-sectional summary data only: No trial-level temporal information or learning effects visible.",
    "Extreme outliers in Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target may drive mean differences; medians more robust but unavailable in summary.",
    "Success as binary precludes direct ANOVA; dichotomization of continuous metrics possible but not shown."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMM) with Mouse as random intercept and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD; use generalized linear mixed model (GLMM, binomial) for Success. This accounts for non-independence across trials within mice. Alternatively, aggregate to mouse-paradigm means (n=8×5=40) and run ANOVA on subject-level data to satisfy independence."
}
